title: query_datasource tool result
description: The structuredContent that the Source gives to the App.

alternatives.description: Each other chart that fits the frames. The App can switch to one with no new query.

grafanaUrl.description: The base URL of the Grafana that the Source queries.

panelId.$comment: Generated from registry/panel-types.json. Do not edit.

panel.description: The panel ID and the options preset of the chart, and the unit and the title of the tool arguments. The panel of the chart also has the options and the fieldConfig of the tool arguments.

title.$comment: Generated from registry/constants.json (maxTitleChars). Do not edit.
title.description: The title of the tool arguments.

range.description: The absolute time range of the query, in epoch milliseconds.

capturedAt.description: The time when the response of /api/ds/query arrived, in epoch milliseconds.

results.description: The results object of the /api/ds/query response, with no change. The key is the refId.

frame.description: A frame in the DataFrameJSON format of the dataplane contract.

query-datasource-args.properties.type.$comment: Generated from registry/chart-types.json. Do not edit.
query-datasource-args.properties.type.description: Optional chart to draw. With no type, the chart comes from the data. Each chart needs: timeseries (a time field and number fields), barchart (number fields, with a string or time field for the categories), histogram (number fields), candlestick (number fields named open, high, low and close), boxplot (number fields named min, q1, median, q3 and max), piechart (a number field, with a string field for the names of the parts), funnel (a number field, with a string field for the names of the stages), heatmap (heatmap cells, or a time field and number fields for the buckets), geomap (a geo field, a geohash field, or latitude and longitude fields), state-timeline (a time field and string, boolean or number fields), status-history (a time field and string, boolean or number fields), nodeGraph (node graph frames, or source and target fields), sankey (source, target and value fields), chord (source, target and value fields), treemap (string fields for the levels and a number field), sunburst (string fields for the levels and a number field), radar (three or more number fields), parallel (two or more number fields), streamgraph (a time field and number fields), bubble (a time field and number fields).
